nodes.label: Eywa Heterogeneous Agentic Framework
nodes.author: Li et al.
nodes.rationale: Framework enabling LLM agents to collaborate with domain-specific foundation models through FM-LLM 'Tsaheylu' interface; addresses language-centric bottleneck in scientific agentic systems.

nodes.label: FM-LLM Tsaheylu Interface
nodes.rationale: Bidirectional communication interface with query compiler (ϕ: state→FM config) and response adapter (ψ: FM output→language context); implemented via Model Context Protocol (MCP).

nodes.label: EywaAgent: Single-Agent Integration
nodes.rationale: Coupled FM-LLM unit with control policy deciding invoke/skip; enables adaptive switching between generalized reasoning and specialized acting; subsumes language-only agents as special case.

nodes.label: EywaMAS: Multi-Agent Composition
nodes.rationale: Plug-and-play multi-agent system mixing LLM agents and EywaAgents; enables parallel specialization and cross-domain collaboration with fixed communication topology.

nodes.label: EywaOrchestra: Dynamic Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Dynamically instantiated heterogeneous multi-agent system with conductor selecting agent roles, LLM backbones, FMs, and topologies per task; enables task-adaptive system construction.

nodes.label: EywaBench: Multi-Domain Scientific Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Scalable benchmark spanning physical/life/social sciences with natural language, time series, and tabular modalities; 200 task instances from 67 source datasets with unified utility metric.

nodes.label: Chronos Time Series Foundation Model
nodes.rationale: General-purpose foundation model for time series forecasting; lacks native language interface but provides strong zero-shot capabilities; integrated via Tsaheylu.

nodes.label: TabPFN Tabular Foundation Model
nodes.rationale: Transformer-based FM using in-context learning for tabular prediction; solves problems in single forward pass; integrated as specialized expert in Eywa systems.

nodes.label: Domain Advantage Assumption
nodes.rationale: Theoretical assumption: domain-specific FMs achieve strictly better performance than language-only models on domain-specific components; justifies heterogeneous collaboration.

nodes.label: Language Interface Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Information-theoretic analysis: serialization of non-linguistic inputs into language tokens discards task-relevant information; data processing inequality shows irreducible Bayes risk gap.

nodes.label: Token Complexity Analysis
nodes.rationale: EywaAgent token cost O(L_call + L_ψ(o_k)) independent of modality size vs. Θ(L(x_k)) for LLM-only; explains ~30% token reduction in practice.

nodes.label: Empirical Performance Gains
nodes.rationale: EywaAgent: +6.6% utility, -30% tokens, -10% latency vs baseline; EywaMAS outperforms homogeneous MAS; EywaOrchestra reaches near-EywaMAS utility with -26% tokens.

nodes.label: Theorem 3: EywaAgent Improvement
nodes.rationale: Formal result: EywaAgent achieves strictly lower optimal risk than language-only agents under domain advantage assumption; expands solvable task space.

nodes.label: Theorem 17: EywaMAS Solvability
nodes.rationale: Single EywaAgent in EywaMAS propagates recovered information through communication graph; achieves zero risk on task families where LLM-only MAS remains constrained.

nodes.label: Theorem 18: Adaptive Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Oracle adaptive routing strictly improves over best fixed configuration when different task regions favor different configurations; motivates EywaOrchestra.

nodes.label: GPT-5-nano Language Model
nodes.rationale: Default LLM backbone for Eywa experiments; provides general-purpose reasoning interface for coordinating domain-specific foundation models.

nodes.label: Case Study A: Time Series Forecasting
nodes.rationale: LLM-only agent collapses to persistence baseline (0.605 utility); EywaAgent with Chronos achieves 0.701 by delegating core prediction to FM while LLM handles interface.

nodes.label: Case Study B: Tabular Regression
nodes.rationale: EywaOrchestra planner identifies Miami house-price task as tabular, selects single-agent config with TabPFN; achieves 0.853 utility by avoiding unnecessary multi-agent discussion.

nodes.label: Model Context Protocol Implementation
nodes.rationale: Tsaheylu instantiated via MCP; FMs exposed as remote services with defined input/output schemas; query compiler produces structured tool calls; response adapter transforms outputs.

nodes.label: Pareto Frontier Analysis
nodes.rationale: Eywa methods consistently sit on Pareto frontier across all 9 sub-domains; LLM-only MAS baselines dominated; demonstrates utility-token trade-off superiority.

nodes.label: Hyperparameter Robustness
nodes.rationale: Eywa stable across LLM temperature, FM temperature, and prompt designs; gains not tied to specific hyperparameter choices; robust to design variations.

nodes.label: LLM Backbone Ablation
nodes.rationale: Eywa effective across gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-5-nano, gpt-5-mini; benefits from stronger LLMs but gains primarily from FM-LLM coupling not backbone scale.

nodes.label: Diminishing Returns from LLM Scaling
nodes.rationale: gpt-4.1-nano→gpt-5-nano: +15.5% utility; gpt-5-nano→gpt-5-mini: +1.25%; indicates domain-specific capability becomes bottleneck after sufficient LLM reasoning ability.
